place.name: The Taj Mahal
place.context: A mausoleum commissioned by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, built from 1632 to 1653. Photographed from the 1850s by John Murray, then Samuel Bourne and Lala Deen Dayal.

story.title: The Taj Mahal, Agra – 1880
story.en: As general context, Agra in 1880 remained a city shaped by its Mughal past. The Taj Mahal stood on a platform measuring 300 metres in length on the banks of the Yamuna river [S9]. As general context, it continued to draw visitors and photographers. It was commissioned in 1631 by the fifth Mughal emperor, Shah Jahan, to house the tomb of his late wife Mumtaz Mahal [S9]. Construction started in 1632, and the mausoleum was completed in 1648, while the surrounding buildings and garden were finished five years later [S9]. It is a white marble structure standing on a 6-metre high square plinth with sides measuring 95.5 metres in length [S9]. The four minarets, which are each more than 40 metres tall, are symmetrically arranged on the corners facing the chamfered corners of the main building [S9]. As general context, views of the monument from the river and gardens were already well known through photographs.
story.fr: Comme contexte général, Agra en 1880 restait une ville façonnée par son passé moghol. Le Taj Mahal se dressait sur une plate-forme mesurant 300 mètres de long sur les rives de la rivière Yamuna [S9]. Comme contexte général, il continuait d'attirer visiteurs et photographes. Il fut commandé en 1631 par le cinquième empereur moghol, Shah Jahan, pour abriter le tombeau de sa défunte épouse Mumtaz Mahal [S9]. La construction commença en 1632, et le mausolée fut achevé en 1648, tandis que les bâtiments environnants et le jardin furent terminés cinq ans plus tard [S9]. C'est une structure en marbre blanc reposant sur un socle carré de 6 mètres de haut dont les côtés mesurent 95,5 mètres de long [S9]. Les quatre minarets, qui mesurent chacun plus de 40 mètres de haut, sont disposés symétriquement aux angles face aux angles chanfreinés du bâtiment principal [S9]. Comme contexte général, les vues du monument depuis la rivière et les jardins étaient déjà bien connues grâce aux photographies.

events.text: Each side of the iwan is framed with a 33-metre (108 ft) high pishtaq (vaulted archway) with two similarly shaped arched balconies stacked on either side.
The four minarets, which are each more than 40 metres (130 ft) tall, are symmetrically arranged on the corners facing the chamfered corners of the main building.
The base structure is a large multi-chambered cube with chamfered corners forming an eight-sided structure that is approximately 57.3 metres (188 ft) long on each of the four long sides.
It is a white marble structure standing on a 6-metre (20 ft) high square plinth with sides measuring 95.5 metres (313 ft) in length.
The entire complex sits on a platform measuring 300 metres (980 ft) in length and 8.7 metres (28.5 ft) in height on the banks of the Yamuna river.
It was commissioned in 1631 by the fifth Mughal emperor, Shah Jahan (r. 1628–1658), to house the tomb of his late wife, Mumtaz Mahal; it also houses the tomb of Shah Jahan himself.
Construction started in 1632, and the mausoleum was completed in 1648, while the surrounding buildings and garden were finished five years later.
Abdul Hamid Lahori, in his 1636 book Padshahnama, refers to the Taj Mahal as rauza-i munawwara (Perso-Arabic: روضه منواره, rawdah-i munawwarah), meaning the illumined or illustrious tomb.
The first ceremony held at the mausoleum was an observance by Shah Jahan, on 6 February 1643, of the 12th anniversary of the death of Mumtaz Mahal.
Construction of the mausoleum was completed in 1648, although work on other parts of the complex continued for another five years.

events.label: 19th c.
events.text: As the Mughal Empire declined, the gardens were not maintained, and when the British Raj assumed management of the gardens, they changed the landscaping to resemble the formal lawns of London in the 19th century.
Since Indian independence in 1947, the Archaeological Survey of India has been responsible for the maintenance of the monument.
The Taj Mahal was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 for being "the jewel of Muslim art in India and one of the universally admired masterpieces of the world's heritage".

In 2005, a similar petition brought by Amar Nath Mishra, a social worker and preacher claiming that the Taj Mahal was built by the Hindu king Paramardi in 1196, was dismissed by the Allahabad High Court.
In 2007, it was declared a winner of the New 7 Wonders of the World initiative.
According to a 2025 government report, the Taj Mahal earned ₹297 crore (US$31 million) over five years, making it the highest-earning ASI monument.

history.intro: The Taj Mahal ( TAHJ mə-HAHL, TAHZH -⁠; Hindustani: [t̪ɑːd͡ʒ ˈmɛɦ(ɛ)l]; lit. 'Crown of the Palace') is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the river Yamuna in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India. It was commissioned in 1631 by the fifth Mughal emperor, Shah Jahan (r. 1628–1658), to house the tomb of his late wife, Mumtaz Mahal; it also houses the tomb of Shah Jahan himself. The tomb is the centrepiece of a 17-hectare (42-acre) complex, which includes a mosque and a guest house, and is set in formal gardens bounded on three sides by a crenellated wall.
